value_chain.value_chain_position: Core model creation and open-weight distribution layer. Meta AI depends on NVIDIA GPUs (1.5M+ GPU fleet by early 2026, heavily featuring Blackwell B200 and GB200) and third-party cloud providers for training infrastructure, with $72.2B in AI capex in 2025 and $115-135B planned for 2026. Its open-weight Llama models serve the broadest downstream ecosystem in AI: thousands of developers, enterprises, cloud providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Together AI), and even national governments (France, India, UAE) build on Llama. Meta AI also powers Meta's own consumer products (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, Ray-Ban Meta glasses). Unlike closed model creators, Meta's primary monetization is indirect -- Llama improves Meta's core advertising business rather than generating direct model revenue.

key_products: Llama model family (Llama 4 Scout, Maverick, Behemoth): open-weight foundation models. Scout (17B active / 109B total params, 10M token context), Maverick (17B active / 400B total params, 1M context), Behemoth (288B active / 2T total params, in development). First MoE architecture Llama models with native multimodal support. Available for download and self-hosting under Llama Community License.

Meta AI assistant: consumer AI assistant built on Llama, integrated across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. Available in 40+ countries. Powers conversational AI, image understanding, content creation, and real-time visual assistance on smart glasses.

AI infrastructure and developer tools (Llama API, AI Studio, PyTorch): Meta previewed a first-party Llama API (Apr 2025), launched AI Studio for AI character creation, and maintains PyTorch -- the dominant open-source deep learning framework used by the majority of AI researchers and developers worldwide.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Meta Platforms (parent) reported $200.97B total revenue in 2025 (up 22% YoY), passing $200B annual revenue for the first time. Meta AI does not report standalone revenue. The Advantage+ AI-driven ad platform reached a $60B annual run rate in 2025. Market cap: ~$1.8T (Jan 2026). Meta's AI investments are monetized primarily through improved ad targeting and user engagement across its family of apps.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: Not separately disclosed for Meta AI. Meta's overall revenue is primarily advertising-based (not subscription ARR). Meta is beginning to explore paid tiers for Meta AI assistants and enterprise Llama support, but no standalone ARR figures have been disclosed. Revenue from Llama API and enterprise licensing is nascent.
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Not applicable -- Meta AI is a division of Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ: META), a publicly traded company. Not separately funded. Meta invested $72.2B in AI infrastructure capex in 2025 and plans $115-135B for 2026. Meta also invested $14.3B in Scale AI (2025) as part of talent acquisition strategy. Between 2022-2025, Meta spent roughly $140B on AI-related projects cumulatively.
business.business_model: Indirect monetization through AI-enhanced advertising (primary). Meta AI's models improve ad targeting, content recommendation, and user engagement across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, driving Meta's $200B+ advertising revenue. Secondary revenue streams: (1) Llama licensing for enterprises exceeding 700M MAU (requires custom license from Meta); (2) Revenue-sharing agreements with cloud hosting partners (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure); (3) Emerging Llama API and enterprise support tiers (launched 2025); (4) Meta does not charge for Llama model weights below the 700M MAU threshold.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Not applicable in startup terms -- Meta Platforms is profitable with $200.97B revenue and strong operating margins. However, AI-specific spending is enormous: $72.2B capex in 2025, $115-135B planned for 2026. Reality Labs (AR/VR division) continues to lose ~$16B/year. Meta's AI infrastructure buildout represents the largest AI investment of any company besides Alphabet.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Open-weight (restrictive). Llama models are released under the Llama Community License, which allows free commercial use, fine-tuning, and derivative works, but with restrictions: (1) Companies exceeding 700M MAU must obtain a separate license from Meta; (2) The Open Source Initiative (OSI) has repeatedly stated Llama does not meet the Open Source Definition due to use restrictions; (3) Derivative models must include 'Llama' in their name and display 'Built with Llama' branding; (4) Starting with Llama 3.1, training on Llama outputs is permitted with attribution; (5) Llama 4 Community License does not grant rights to EU-domiciled individuals or companies with EU principal place of business (a controversial restriction). PyTorch, by contrast, is fully open-source under BSD license.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: Meta AI is arguably the most important company for startups seeking independence from proprietary AI providers. Key considerations: (1) Llama is the leading open-weight model family, enabling startups to self-host, fine-tune, and customize foundation models without per-token API costs -- this fundamentally changes unit economics for AI-native companies; (2) The 700M MAU licensing threshold is irrelevant for virtually all startups, making Llama effectively free for commercial use; (3) The open-weight approach gives startups data sovereignty and privacy control that closed APIs cannot match -- critical for regulated industries (healthcare, finance, defense); (4) Llama is available on 25+ cloud providers (AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, Azure, Together AI, Groq, etc.), preventing vendor lock-in and enabling multi-cloud strategies; (5) 'Llama for Startups' program (May 2025) offers Meta team support and potential funding for Llama-native companies; (6) CRITICAL WARNING for EU startups: Llama 4 Community License explicitly excludes EU-domiciled entities -- French and European startups must negotiate custom licenses or use alternative models (Mistral, Gemma); (7) PyTorch (maintained by Meta) is the de facto standard ML framework -- virtually every AI startup depends on it; (8) Meta's indirect monetization model means it has less incentive to compete with startups building on Llama (unlike OpenAI/Google which sell competing products directly); (9) The MoE architecture in Llama 4 enables running large models with smaller active parameter counts, reducing inference costs for startups.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Very high accessibility for non-EU entities. Llama model weights are freely downloadable from llama.com and Hugging Face. Self-hosting eliminates per-token costs (pay only for compute). API access available through 25+ cloud partners at competitive pricing ($0.10-$0.90 per M tokens depending on model and provider). No Meta-specific startup credit program, but Llama is included in AWS Activate, Google for Startups, and Azure startup programs. 'Llama for Startups' program offers technical support and potential investment. EU accessibility is restricted: Llama 4 license excludes EU-domiciled entities, requiring custom license negotiation.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None. Meta AI is a foundation model creator.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: Cloud distribution partners: AWS (Bedrock), Google Cloud (Vertex AI), Microsoft Azure, Together AI, Groq, and 20+ other providers hosting Llama models. NVIDIA (primary GPU supplier: 1.5M+ GPU fleet). Scale AI ($14.3B investment, 2025). National AI partnerships: France, India, UAE using Llama as backbone for national AI initiatives. Hardware partnerships: Qualcomm, MediaTek for on-device Llama deployment. Ray-Ban/EssilorLuxottica for Meta smart glasses with Llama-powered AI. Open-source ecosystem: PyTorch Foundation, Hugging Face as primary distribution platform.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Open-weight ecosystem dominance: Llama is the most widely deployed open-weight model family, creating a massive developer ecosystem and community moat that is self-reinforcing. Platform distribution: Meta AI assistant integrated across Facebook (3B+ MAU), Instagram (2B+ MAU), WhatsApp (2B+ MAU), reaching more users than any competing AI assistant. Data advantage: Meta's social media platforms generate unparalleled user interaction data for training and improving AI models. PyTorch lock-in: as maintainer of the dominant ML framework, Meta shapes the entire AI development ecosystem. Scale economics: 1.5M+ GPU fleet and $72B+ annual AI capex create compute scale few can match. Open-weight strategy makes Llama the default alternative to proprietary models, establishing it as critical infrastructure.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: GPAI provider with systemic risk, but non-compliant posture. Meta has publicly refused to sign the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice. Joel Kaplan (Meta's chief global affairs officer) stated 'Europe is heading down the wrong path on AI' (Jul 2025). Llama 3.1-405B exceeds the 10^25 FLOPs threshold for systemic risk classification under the EU AI Act. Despite the confrontational stance, Meta offered EU institutions access to Llama for national security purposes (Sep 2025). The Llama 4 Community License explicitly excludes EU-domiciled users, creating a regulatory grey zone. Meta's open-weight approach may qualify for certain GPAI exemptions under the EU AI Act's open-source provisions, but the restrictive license terms complicate this argument. This adversarial regulatory posture is important context for Session 5 ethics discussion.
